title: Ownership and free
goal: Identify one owner of an allocation and release it exactly once on both use and rejection paths.

prerequisites.text: Check malloc before accessing the result.
Understand passing the address of a variable to a function.

terms.title: Owner
terms.definition: The variable the program makes responsible for releasing the allocation. This is a program convention.

terms.title: Borrow
terms.definition: Temporary access without taking responsibility for release.

terms.title: Cleanup
terms.definition: Ending use of the resource. Pointers to the old block are not used after free.

sections.title: An allocation's lifetime and its owner
paragraphs: In the teaching program owner is responsible for the allocation. view_total gets temporary access for reading, with no responsibility or permission to release the block.

The call release_values(&owner, &releases) passes the addresses of two live variables. Inside the function, the parameter owner has type int **, and *owner is the pointer value held by main. If *owner is NULL, there is no block to release. Otherwise the function calls free, sets the variable in main to NULL, and counts one release.
After free, do not evaluate old pointer copies. Storing NULL updates only the owner variable. In this example, temporary access ends when view_total returns.
releases counts block releases, not calls to the function. That is an observable check of the shared cleanup path.

sections.title: Check the cleanup twice safely
paragraphs: Predict when free is called and what view_total reads.
steps: owner stores [4, 5] and lends temporary access to view_total.
The first release_values frees the block, writes NULL, and increments the counter.
The second call never reads the old block. The program prints releases 1.

sections.title: Locate and check the defect
paragraphs: If Clang reports too few arguments, compare the call with the release_values declaration. It requires both the address of the owner variable &owner and the address of the actual-release counter.
Increment the counter after free, inside the *owner != NULL branch. The second call sees the NULL already stored in the owner variable.

sections.title: Change, predict and check
paragraphs: Explain what happens if main returns before cleanup on rejection. Use a state diagram rather than running a version that loses its owner.
Add a second way to reject the computation while preserving one cleanup path.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Review the language and library contracts used in this example.

selfcheck.prompt: What does the final printf in the example print?
feedback: The first call sees a non-null owner.
The second call skips release after the NULL assignment.
The call count differs from the release count.

selfcheck.prompt: Who releases the array in the example?
options: Any function that sees its values.
The function that receives temporary read access.
The designated owner through the cleanup operation.
feedback: Seeing the data and owning the allocation are different contracts.
One release point makes the lifetime checkable.

selfcheck.prompt: Why should released still be 1 in mode 0 when no sum is printed?
selfcheck.feedback: The buffer has already been allocated and initialized. Rejecting a calculation does not remove the need to release it.

practice.title: Two paths, one release
practice.task: The first line of up to 63 bytes contains count from 1 to 16 and a mode of 0 or 1. The array is allocated and filled with 1 through count before the mode is checked. Mode 1 prints sum N. Mode 0 rejects the calculation and prints rejected. Both branches must free the allocated block. Complete the counter in release_values. Two cleanup calls should yield released 1. Invalid input prints invalid and released 0. If the initial malloc returns NULL, the program prints allocation-failed and released 0.
criteria: 3 1 and 3 0 finish with released 1. 0 1 finishes with released 0.
The borrower does not free the block. Cleanup stores NULL before a possible repeated call.
practice.hint: Increment the counter after free inside the non-null owner branch only.

steps.action: Run the starter with 3 1 and find the TODO in release_values.
steps.why: The block is freed without incrementing the counter.

steps.action: After the fix, run 3 1, 3 0, and 0 1 separately.
steps.why: Mode 0 rejects the calculation after allocation. A count of 0 is rejected before allocation.
steps.expected: The line pairs are sum 6 and released 1, rejected and released 1, and invalid and released 0.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: In a separate copy, also reject the calculation when count is even. Keep the shared release path.
criteria: With 4 1 the new branch rejects the computation, while released 1 remains. Name the single owner.

teaching.scene: A report handles measurements on both success and rejection paths. Use the release count to verify that either path leaves the owner with no allocated block.

predict.prompt: owner holds 4 and 5. After view_total, release_values runs twice. What do the two printf calls print, and when does the owner's pointer become NULL?
predict.answer: It prints total 9 and releases 1. The first call releases the live block, resets the owner's pointer and increments the count. The second sees NULL and changes nothing.

apply.prompt: For five elements, compare modes 1 and 0 assuming initial allocation succeeds. What part of the report must be the same after two cleanup calls?
apply.answer: Mode 1 prints sum 15 and mode 0 prints rejected. Both end with released 1 because each path releases the allocated block once.

practice.strategy: Identify the owner after allocation and when borrowed access ends. Bring both branches to cleanup and count only an actual release.
practice.diagnosis: With 3 1 the starter gives sum 6 and released 0. The sum is correct. The block is freed, but the counter fails to record that event.

syntax.explanation: Pass &owner and the address of the counter as valid parameters. Resetting through int ** updates the caller's variable, so the next cleanup sees NULL.
syntax.mistake: Resetting the owner does not update other pointers to the same block. Borrowed pointers must no longer be used after free.
